scope.evidence_basis: Author derivation and rereading of diagonal extraction, derivative compatibility, Holder interpolation, quadratic-form passage and continuity on the admissible domain.

N-main: Import the exact strong C^{2,beta} compactness interface, without claiming its proof here.
Pass the uniform matrix lower bound to the limit.
Use admissibility and operator continuity to pass the equation.
Import the exact strong C^{2,beta} compactness interface, without claiming its full proof here.

N-main.objects: Periodic real functions, the continuous symmetric-matrix map A, its positive domain U, and the continuous equation map F are explicitly declared.
N-main.domain: Integers d,r>=1, 0<beta<alpha<1, fixed flat torus, parameter interval [0,1] and the target C0 spaces are retained.
N-main.fixed_and_variable: A,F and norms are fixed. t_j,u_j are a given sequence; only a subsequence and its limit are concluded.
N-main.hypotheses: Continuity, an already existing solution sequence, uniform C2alpha bound and one positive delta independent of j and x are all present.
N-main.equations: The equation F(t_j,u_j)=0 and all norm/matrix inequalities are displayed. Norms are defined completely immediately before the theorem, not by a remote label.
N-main.quantifiers: The constants are independent of j; the matrix bound is for every j,x; the conclusion is some subsequence, not the entire sequence.
N-main.conclusion: The limit is C2alpha, convergence is C2beta, the margin persists and the equation holds; no smoothness or new existence claim.
N-main.status: A proved conditional closedness lemma for the stated data, not a solution of a nonlinear existence problem.
N-main.local_definitions: The flat distance, derivatives, Holder seminorm and norm are displayed immediately before each principal; symmetric-matrix order is quadratic-form order, recalled locally.
